To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein expression of human peripheral neutrophil is differentially modulated by GM-CSF and TNFRα and that this modulation can serve as a biomarker for the in vivo action of these cytokine in chronic inflammatory disease.
GM-CSF and TNFGα modulate protein profiles in neutrophils, which might serve as biomarkers of neutrophil activation in vivo.
the cytokine-induced protein expression profiles of neutrophils, visualized by 2D-fluorescence difference gel electropheresis (2D DIGE), can be used as biomarkers for their action in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of protein markers of human peripheral neutrophil function.

the identification of biomarkers that are indicative for the presence of specific cytokines in the blood and the development of a diagnostic assay for the detection of cytokine-induced biomarker profiles.
the analysis of cytokine-induced protein expression in neutrophils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GM-CSF and TNFA modulate the protein expression in human neutrophils.
the protein profiles of neutrophils induced by TNFalpha and GM-CSF were not identical.
2D-DGE analysis of human peripheral blood neutrophils is a useful tool in the study of the action of cytokines on these cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
2D-DIFGE is a useful technique to identify proteins that can be used as biomarkers for neutrophil activation in vivo.
the cytokine-regulated proteins can be used as biomarkers for peripheral neutrophils activation.

the protein profile of human neutrophil stimulation by GM-CSF is a promising tool for the identification of neutrophil activation in vivo, whereas TNFα does not induce a protein profile that can be used as biomarker for its action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteome of human neutrophil can be analyzed in a quantitative manner by 2D DIGE.
the proteomic approach is a powerful tool to study neutrophils in health and disease.
2D-DIFGE can be used to study the action of individual inflammatory cytokines in neutrophils.
